Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register and then press the star key followed by the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star 2. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are David Kwon, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Elena Vasquez, CTO; Mike Thornton, Chief Revenue Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Kwon.

David Kwon:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on six key areas: sales efficiency, full-year revenue guidance, ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, MRR trends, customer mix, and operating expense breakdown.

These priorities have positioned us strongly for sustained growth in the competitive RevOps landscape, where our AI-powered platform—delivering next-gen CRM orchestration, predictive analytics, no-code workflow automation, and DevOps/CI/CD capabilities—continues to resonate with mid-market enterprises of 500 to 5,000 employees. We're outperforming peers like Salesforce Einstein, HubSpot, Outreach, Snowflake, and GitLab through our land-and-expand model and consistent net revenue retention above 120%.

We're confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $352 million, representing a 36% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 79%, and non-GAAP operating income was $98 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at over $850 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

To provide deeper insight into the six key areas David highlighted, let's start with sales efficiency, a cornerstone metric for scaling SaaS businesses like ours. For context, CloudForge offers an AI-powered revenue operations platform with embedded predictive analytics, no-code workflows, and DevOps integrations, competing effectively in a crowded field. Our Rule of 40 score reached 68% this quarter, with our magic number at 1.3x, improved from 1.1x last year.

On sales cycle length, our quarter-weighted average from lead qualification to close-won is now 92 days, a 23% improvement year-over-year from 120 days and 8% shorter sequentially from Q2's 100 days. This places us in the top quartile for mid-market SaaS per Bessemer benchmarks. By segment, SMB and mid-market under $100K ARR averaged 65 days, down 15% YoY, thanks to product-led growth from our freemium self-serve tier that converts 40% of trials to paid in 14 days. Enterprise over $100K ARR is at 145 days, 18% better YoY, aided by multi-threaded selling despite IT budget scrutiny.

Regionally, North America leads at 85 days, EMEA at 105 days with improvements from localized German and French content boosting pilots 30%, and APAC at 130 days, shortened 20% QoQ via AWS Marketplace Japan partnerships. Key drivers include our ForgeAI lead scoring with ZoomInfo and 6sense cutting disqualification by 35%, virtual demo automation via Gong reducing POC phases from 45 to 25 days, and DocuSign-Ironclad integrations saving 10 days on contracts. Amid macro thaw post-Fed signals, inbound leads form 65% of pipeline.

Shifting to conversion rates, MQL to closed-won is 4.2%, up from 3.1% YoY, above the 3-5% SaaS median and fueling $28 million in new ARR, 25% above guide. Funnel details: MQL to SQL at 28%, up 5 points from ABM and 92% accurate ICP scoring; SQL to opportunity at 62%, up 8 points with 120 inside reps and 45% PLG opps; opportunity to close-won at 38%, up 7 points from 55% analytics module attach. Overall inbound PLG wins at 45%, outbound enterprise at 32%. NA at 5.1%, EMEA 3.8%, APAC 2.9% up 50% YoY. Amplifiers: Clari-Salesloft stack boosting closes 12%, self-serve upsells at 35% contributing 22% ARR, and RevOps buyer focus widening funnel 18%.

Overall, this yields a 4.2x sales multiple with 122% NRR and 4% churn. We're investing $15 million in sales tech like Chorus.ai for sub-85-day cycles, hedging macro risks with 35% PLG revenue and Forge Accelerate partner program like ServiceNow's.

Next, turning to ARR growth. ARR ended Q3 at $258 million, up 39% year-over-year from $185 million, ahead of guide and reflecting strength in a stabilizing IT budget environment akin to GitLab and Harness. Sequentially, up 6.2% from $243 million in Q2, our strongest QoQ in three quarters.

Net new ARR of $73 million breaks down to $28 million new logos, 38% of total and up 45% YoY with 17 deals over $1 million ACV like a Fortune 50 financial services Kubernetes deployment; average ACV $420K up 12% from GenAI PipelineForge at 95% attach. Expansion $52 million, 71% of net new and 52% YoY growth, DBNER 118% above Bessemer 110% average, driven by SecurityForge and ObservabilityForge upsells. Churn negative $7 million or -10%, gross retention 98%, net 122%, limited to two SMB M&A cases offset by AI health scoring.

Regions: NA $175 million or 68%, up 42%; EMEA $57 million or 22%, 48% YoY; APAC $26 million or 10%, 25% YoY and 12% QoQ with Tokyo data center. This underscores AI-native DevOps investments of $15 million, 85% expansions tied to LLMs, LTV/CAC 4.2x. Q4 expects low-30s YoY, 6-7% QoQ toward $350 million FY25 start.

Moving to MRR trends, ending MRR hit $45.2 million, up 28% YoY from $35.1 million—strongest in five quarters, accelerating from Q2's 24%—and 5.2% QoQ ahead of our 4.5-5% guide, on track for 26% full-year growth despite elongated cycles like at Atlassian and ServiceNow.

Components: new logo MRR $4.2 million up 15% sequentially from mid-market $25K ACV with CI/CD-GenAI bundles competing GitHub Copilot Enterprise; expansion $3.1 million with 112% NRR up from 110%, 8% dollar net expansion, 85% renewals over 36 months via outcome pricing. Churn: 97% gross dollar retention, under 2% logo churn over $100K ARR, down 22% at-risk via ForgeGuard AI.

Regions: Americas $27.1 million or 60%, 30% YoY from AWS Outposts-Snowflake integrations and six $500K+ Fortune 500 deals; EMEA $11.3 million or 25%, 25% YoY with Frankfurt-Dublin edges, 115% NRR in automotive packs; APAC $6.8 million or 15%, 35% YoY and 8.2% QoQ from Singapore hub, Mandarin AI, 13 $100K+ Japan-India wins.

Bets: AI at 40% new MRR, 1.8x expansions, 5-7% pricing uplift adding $1.2 million. Q4 5.5-6% QoQ for $47.5-47.8 million FY25 start, Rule of 40 mid-50s.

On customer mix, enterprise (ACV >$100K, Fortune 1000 equivalents) is 68% of $420 million total ARR at $285 million, up from 60% YoY and growing 28%, while SMB 32% or $135 million grows 12%. Enterprise NRR 122% with 18% expansions from AI predictive analytics like Einstein but no-code integrated; cohorts up 35% seats/modules, sub-3% churn vs. industry 8-10%.

SMB moderated in high rates, NRR 108% from 112%, 5% churn from fintech/e-comm consolidation, but 15,000 net logos via freemium at 28% paid conversion with Twilio nudges. Regions: NA 52% ARR, 75% enterprise like $5M bank fraud deal; EMEA 28% ARR, 55/45 mix with 40 new enterprise telco logos; APAC 20% ARR, 65% enterprise up from 50% via AWS Outposts; LatAm SMB-heavy.

Enterprise sales up 25% capacity, 6-9 month cycles with SAs for ServiceNow-Databricks syncs; SMB CAC down 22% PQLs, usage pricing pilots. Enterprise to 75% ARR by FY26, $1B+ with 115%+ NRR like Workday pivot.

Finally, operating expense breakdown. Non-GAAP opex $192 million or 67% revenue, down 300bps YoY for Rule of 40 at 85 (28% growth, 57% EBITDA margin). R&D $68 million or 24% flat YoY%, up 22% absolute via Bangalore-Tel Aviv 35% headcount; 40% or $27M to NovaAI Copilot agentic workflows, AWS Bedrock-Azure OpenAI cutting costs 30%, EMEA GDPR localization up 15% QoQ; Q4 to 25-26% for multi-modal AI vs. Anthropic in Einstein, 20% more features/eng, 125% NRR ROI.

Sales & Marketing $85 million or 30%, down 450bps YoY/200bps QoQ, 12% absolute growth; CAC payback 14 months from 18, LTV:CAC 4.2x like Snowflake. Cut perf marketing 20% to $12M for freemium 40% new ARR, inside SMB +35%, 60% bookings expansions; APAC $18M up 25% Japan-Aus; AI copilots cut rep ramp to 60 days, channel expansion AWS-GCP for $50M partner ARR.

G&A $39 million or 14%, down 150bps YoY, 8% growth; SBC 7% revenue, fees $8M audit; Dublin compliance +10% QoQ, people 55% via Rippling; target sub-13% FY25 with AI contract bots -40% review.

This discipline fuels 60%+ EBITDA next year amid headwinds.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.38 billion to $1.42 billion, as detailed in the land-and-expand drivers, with subscription $1.27-$1.30 billion, ARR end $1.55-$1.60 billion or 37-42% YoY; prof services $110-$120M; regions NA $960-$990M 36%, EMEA $280-$290M 28%, APAC $140-$150M 55%; non-GAAP op margins 28-30%, FCF 32%, Rule of 60 at 65 Q2. Assumes no macro deterioration, stress-tested cycles, multi-cloud edge.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including 99.99% uptime and sub-100ms latency.

And now Lisa Patel will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Elena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of NovaAI Copilot. This new feature significantly improves agentic workflow automation and real-time anomaly detection, reducing time-to-value by 40%. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy, with 150% QoQ beta uptake among Fortune 50 customers.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, please press star 1. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, and how it compares to your initial expectations?

Mike Thornton:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge AI has been transformative for growth, contributing 15% to Q3 bookings and 65% adoption in new logos, with expansions tied 85% to its GenAI layers like GPT and Claude integrations. Attach rates are at 95% in new deals and 55% overall for modules, driving NRR lift of 20-25% in cohorts. This exceeds initial expectations by 25%, mirroring Adobe Firefly, with $40 million committed pipeline 60% expansion-weighted—far ahead of our conservative models.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Kim:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, and what are your key target markets?

David Kwon:
Great question, Laura. International expansion remains a priority, with APAC as our fastest-growing region at 55% YoY revenue growth. Plans include ramping our Singapore hub and Tokyo data center, deepening hyperscaler partnerships like AWS Marketplace generating $25 million Q2 bookings, and localizing AI features in Mandarin. Key targets: Japan and ANZ telcos/financials for cloud-native RevOps, manufacturing verticals with Edge analytics pilots akin to Siemens, and India fintechs—aiming for 20% of ARR by FY25 while navigating forex.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, and what are your strategies to improve customer retention?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Raj. Churn management is robust: gross dollar retention at 97-98%, logo churn under 2-5% segmented, limited to SMB M&A amid rates but offset enterprise stickiness. NRR trends steady at 122-128%, with Q3 at 122%, enterprise 145%, overall 112-118% DBNER. Strategies: ForgeGuard/AI health scoring flags risks 30 days early reducing at-risk 22%; self-serve upsells 35% via in-app, 22% ARR contribution; CS-led expansions 4x churn; multi-year renewals 85%+; PLG onboarding Slack-like for 40% trial conversion. Proactive like Snowflake, de-risking to 35% bookings growth FY24.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Kwon for closing remarks.

David Kwon:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
